NEGATIVE PROMPT: different person, different face, face morphing, identity drift, altered facial structure, different eyes, different nose, different lips, different jawline, different skin tone, different hairstyle, inconsistent body proportions, duplicate person, distorted anatomy, asymmetrical face, plastic skin, waxy skin, CGI, 3D render, cartoon, anime, illustration, over-beautification, excessive makeup, unrealistic eyes, blurry face, low detail, extra fingers, missing fingers, malformed hands, bad anatomy.

OUTPUT: One complete, highly detailed professional CHARACTER CONSISTENCY SHEET in a single image, suitable as a master reference for generating consistent images and videos of this character.

Video created by Seedance 2.5:

SCENE: A day in New York shot entirely by the subject herself: waking in her hotel suite, coffee, getting ready, out into the city, back to the room at night.

ACTIVE REFERENCES: @image1 — the hotel suite. Curved cove ceiling with warm LED coving, deep red carpet, cream walls, two black organic sculptures above a light wood headboard, white bedding with red pillows, twin bedside lamps, pale sofa, oval coffee table, sheer curtains, dark door. @image2 — the subject. Young woman, shoulder-length wavy blonde hair with curtain bangs and highlights, light freckles, thin gold necklace, silver ring, dark brown off-the-shoulder knit with white diamond-stripe pattern. 100% matches the reference.

CAMERA OWNERSHIP LOCK: Only two positions exist. HELD: arm extended, camera 0.4–0.7m from her face, visible arm tension, tilt and step-bounce. PROPPED: camera on a surface she placed it on, crooked and fixed, with her moving in and out of frame. No operator shots, no tracking, nothing she could not have filmed alone.

FORMAT: Eight shots, 30s, seven hard cuts, no fades. Real-time.

0–4s SHOT 1 — PROPPED, morning room. Camera on the sideboard 3m from the bed at 1.1m, static and tilted. The suite matches @image1: cove light on, curtains half open, cool daylight across the red carpet. @image2 is visible at 0.0s, sitting up on the bed edge. She rubs her face and says to the running camera: “It’s seven. In New York. Why am I awake.” She stands and walks out screen-right. HARD CUT.

4–7s SHOT 2 — HELD, window light. Arm’s length, above eye line. She pulls the curtain, squints at the street below, then looks into the lens: “Okay. It’s actually happening.” Arm wobble throughout. HARD CUT.

7–11s SHOT 3 — PROPPED, coffee. Camera on the oval coffee table, low, looking up past a cup. She sits into frame, pours, tastes, and says: “Hotel coffee. We’ll fix that outside.” Steam bends in the light. HARD CUT.

11–15s SHOT 4 — HELD, mirror. Camera at chest height reflected in the suite mirror. She works through her hair with the other hand. At 13s: “This is as good as it gets. Let’s go.” HARD CUT.

15–18s SHOT 5 — HELD, leaving. Camera held low at waist height, turned forward. She crosses the red carpet to the door. She opens it and corridor light floods the frame. Off-frame: “Downtown first.” HARD CUT.

18–22s SHOT 6 — PROPPED, street. Camera on a stoop rail, static and crooked. A New York block behind her: brownstone steps, fire escapes, yellow cabs, steam from a vent. She walks in from screen-left, stands in frame, and says: “Look at this street.” Then walks to the lens and takes it. Passers-by cross the foreground. HARD CUT.

22–26s SHOT 7 — PROPPED, diner. Camera on the counter behind a plate, looking up. She sits into frame, takes a bite, eyes widen, and says: “Okay, that’s the one.” She laughs and keeps eating. HARD CUT.

26–30s SHOT 8 — HELD, night, back in the room. She lies back across the white bedding, hair spread, in the brown knit again. Bedside lamps and cove light are the only sources. Into the lens: “Twenty thousand steps. Everything hurts.” Softer: “Same time tomorrow.” She waves as she lowers the camera. 30.0s black.

LIGHTING: Shots 1–4 use cool daylight from the curtains as key and warm cove LED as fill. Shot 5 uses corridor light. Shots 6–7 use hard street daylight and warm diner practicals. Shot 8 uses lamps and cove light only.

AUDIO: Diegetic only, from the same camera — room tone, footsteps, door, traffic, sirens, steam vents, diner clatter, and wind. Ambience ducks under her lines. No music.

Neck muscles tighten.

THAROG violently throws its head upward.

It unleashes a huge territorial roar.

Chest expands.

Dust shakes from armor and nearby stones.

TRANSITION → As the roar ends, THAROG lowers its head directly toward camera.

00:11–00:12 — SEARCH

CAMERA: Slow push toward THAROG's face.

THAROG lowers its head.

One eye remains injured with the arrow embedded.

The functional eye scans left-to-right.

Its breathing becomes increasingly aggressive.

TRANSITION → Camera moves toward the functional eye until the eye fills frame.

THAROG lowers its massive horns.

Hunter runs left-to-right across uneven terrain.

TRANSITION → Camera gradually falls behind Hunter rather than changing screen direction.

Hunter's boots dominate foreground.

THAROG's enormous legs pound the earth behind him.

The distance decreases.

Hunter jumps over a small rock.

TRANSITION → Camera rises above Hunter as he lands, producing the next overhead view.

00:17–00:18 — REVEAL ESCAPE ROUTE

CAMERA: Rising crane into top-down aerial.

Hunter continues along the SAME path.

THAROG follows.

Ahead, the previously established cliff becomes clearly visible.

Hunter has NOT noticed it yet.

TRANSITION → Camera dives from overhead toward Hunter's front.

00:18–00:19 — THAROG GETS CLOSER

CAMERA: Front-facing tracking shot moving backward.

Hunter runs directly toward camera.

He glances over his shoulder.

THAROG is now frighteningly close behind.

Each footfall shakes the camera.

00:19–00:20 — VIOLENT PURSUIT

No stopping.

No dialogue.

Hunter → THAROG → cave entrance are ALL visible in the SAME composition.

THAROG fills more and more of the exterior background.

Hunter prepares to jump.

THAROG's horns remain lowered.

CRASH.

title: WORLD / SCENE IDENTITY
prompt:
WORLD / SCENE IDENTITY

Masterpiece, best quality, very aesthetic. A quiet open winter landscape during gentle snowfall, covered in deep fresh snow beneath a pale blue-gray sky.

The scene feels soft, peaceful, cold, minimal, and slightly whimsical while remaining natural.

MAIN ANCHOR

One single fluffy adult cat stands in deep snow as the primary focal anchor.

Use natural feline anatomy:

compact body,
short strong legs partly buried in snow,
round face,
upright ears,
thick winter fur,
and one large fluffy tail raised upward.

Keep the cat relatively small within the composition so the snowy environment remains important.

POSE

The cat has just stepped into the deep snow and pauses.

Its front paws are slightly forward.

The body is low because of the snow depth.

The tail rises high and curves naturally upward.

The head is tilted slightly upward as if feeling falling snow on its face.

Keep the posture playful, calm, and believable.

FACE

Use a natural cat face with softly simplified painterly anatomy.

The eyes are gently narrowed or nearly closed from the snow and bright winter light.

Keep the expression peaceful and content rather than cartoonish.

FUR

Use thick gray-brown and cream winter fur with subtle darker tabby markings.

The chest, muzzle, and lower face are lighter.

Snow clings lightly to selected fur edges.

Keep fur grouped into soft painterly masses rather than excessive individual hairs.

CAMERA

Use a vertical environmental composition from a low natural viewpoint near the cat's height.

Keep the cat in the lower-middle portion of the frame.

Reserve a large amount of open pale sky and falling snow above it.

COMPOSITION

Build the visual hierarchy:

soft foreground snow
-> single cat
-> raised fluffy tail
-> falling snow
-> pale distant horizon
-> open winter sky.

Keep the composition sparse and immediately readable.

FOREGROUND

Use broad soft snowdrifts with subtle blue shadows and small depressions made by the cat’s paws.

Avoid unrelated objects or clutter.

BACKGROUND

Use a very distant pale snow-covered ridge or low field boundary.

Keep it soft, simple, and low-contrast.

The background should almost dissolve into the atmospheric blue.

SNOWFALL

Use steady natural snowfall with several depth layers:

larger soft flakes near the camera,
medium flakes around the cat,
smaller faint snow farther away.

Keep the pattern irregular and spacious.

LIGHT

Use broad diffuse winter daylight with abundant ambient fill.

The snow remains luminous but not pure white.

Use pale blue and soft lavender-gray in shadow.

The cat receives soft cool light with restrained warm cream highlights on the face, chest, tail edges, and upper fur.

Keep shadows open and chromatic.

COLOR

BASE:
pale winter blue,
soft blue-gray,
snow white,
muted lavender.

COUNTER:
warm cream,
soft gray-brown,
restrained beige fur tones.

ACCENT:
small pink nose and subtle warm ear interiors.

DEPTH

Create depth through:

foreground snow texture,
cat scale,
layered snowfall,
soft horizon,
and progressive atmospheric fading.

Avoid artificial photographic blur.

GLOBAL VISUAL LANGUAGE

Preserve one clear visual thesis:

one fluffy cat stands happily in deep fresh snow while large soft snowflakes fall through a pale blue winter landscape.

The cat provides emotional presence.

The snow provides atmosphere.

The raised tail provides the strongest silhouette gesture.

Keep the scene minimal, painterly, gentle, and immediately readable at thumbnail scale.

PAINTERLY STYLE

A flat hand-drawn graphic illustration, 2000s.
